ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a comparison table of "location factors," with column items including raw materials, labor force, factory land, fuel, transportation, market, and water source. In the table, the row "location requirements" shows: market is "◎," which is the strongest directional factor; factory land, transportation, and water source are "×," belonging to important factors; raw materials, labor force, and fuel are "○," belonging to general factors. In the figure, the row "local conditions" shows: factory land is "excellent," transportation is "excellent," water source is "excellent," market is "good," while raw materials, labor force, and fuel are "poor." Then reason: This industrial sector is most directed toward the market, and at the same time attaches importance to factory land, transportation, and water source; the locality is excellent in the important conditions of factory land, transportation, and water source, and its market condition is also good, so it has the key foundation for cultivating this industry as a leading industry. When vigorously cultivating it as a leading industry, the reasonable direction should be to concentrate the layout of enterprises, expand the production scale, and improve industrial supporting facilities; the measure "disperse the layout of enterprises and reduce the production scale," which is opposite to this direction, is not conducive to forming economies of scale and industrial agglomeration, and therefore is an unreasonable measure.
